ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an was revealed in portions so the Prophet could recite it gradually for people to absorb; this staging serves creatures’ needs and circumstances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The reason for its revelation in parts is because he can gradually recite it out to his people

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r1.claim: Holding to the Qur'an brings the blessed arrival and recognition of God; severing its rope brings distance, deprivation, and lasting punishment.

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r2.speaker: سلمى
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r2.claim: Salami says sinners should be encouraged by God's vast mercy to turn toward Him, while the righteous should be warned by divine majesty not to trust their deeds.
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r2.anchor: بدكارانرا بشارت دهد بسعت رحمت وكمال عفو ما تا روى بدركاه ما آرند

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r3.claim: The cited Hafiz verse says God's mercy extends to every sinner, so a sinful believer should not despair.
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r3.anchor: رحمت او بهر كنهكارا نست نا اميدى مكن اي دوست كه فاسق باشى

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r4.claim: The cited verse warns that ascetic pride does not reach salvation, while a humble seeker may arrive at the abode of peace.
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r4.anchor: زاهد غرور داشت سلامت نبرد راه رنده ازره نياز بدار السلام رفت

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r5.claim: Qurʾānan is governed by an implied verb explained by farraqnāhu: God sent the Qur'an down in separated portions.

BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r6.claim: Its gradual recitation gives people time, aiding memorization and understanding; it was revealed over 23 years according to wisdom, events, and answers to questions.
BURSEVI:v5p162#2/r6.anchor: أي : مهل وتأن فإنه أيسر للحفظ وأعون على الفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r1.claim: قرآنا is accusative through an implied verb explained by فرقناه, an اشتغال construction; a nominative start is also possible if its indefiniteness has a licensing context.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r1.anchor: نصب بفعل مضمر يفسره قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r2.claim: He attaches the accusative to أرسلناك, as in saying that the Prophet was sent as a mercy and a Qur'an; the author calls this strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r3.claim: He also permits coordination with the كاف in أرسلناك, which the author treats as an astonishing parse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r3.anchor: ومما يقضي منه العجب ما جوزه ابن عطية من نصبه بالعطف على الكاف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r4.claim: He proposes an implied verb indicated by آتينا or أرسلناك, a parse ranked below the initial explanation but above the remaining alternatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : وهو دون الأول وفوق ما عداه إنه منصوب بفعل مضمر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r5.claim: فرقناه means either that God sent it down in successive portions or that the Qur'an distinguishes truth from falsehood, the latter involving an omitted preposition; Ibn Abbas also glosses it as explaining lawful and unlawful rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r5.anchor: أي أنزلناه منجما مفرقا أو فرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r6.claim: He glosses فرقناه as perfected and separated, as in the verse about every wise matter being distinguished.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r6.anchor: أحكمناه وفصلناه كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r7.speaker: علي وابن عباس وأبي وعبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r7.claim: They and other named readers pronounce فرقناه with a doubled rā; it still means gradual revelation, with the doubled form intensifying repeated separation. The author prefers this explanation over the proposed contrast between near and far separation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس وأبي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r8.claim: Other explanations divide the Qur'an into commands, rulings, admonitions, examples, stories, reports, and prophecies; most commentators take gradual revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r8.anchor: وقيل معناه فرقنا آياته بين أمر ونهي وحكم وأحكام ومواعظ وأمثال وقصص

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r9.claim: A report says the whole Qur'an moved from the Preserved Tablet to the angelic scribes in the lower heaven, then Gabriel delivered it to the Prophet in portions over twenty years; variants give twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years after placement in Bayt al-Izza, with al-Bahr attributing the variance to disagreement about the Prophet's age.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r9.anchor: نزل القرآن جملة واحدة من عند الله تعالى من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السفرة الكرام الكاتبين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r10.claim: A report through Qatada says revelation took eighteen years, eight in Mecca and ten after migration; Ibn Atiyya calls this confused and unauthentic, while the relied-on span is twenty-three years.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p187#2/r10.anchor: من طريق قتادة عن الحسن كان يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r1.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r1.claim: A report in al-Bayhaqi says Gabriel delivered the Qur'an five verses at a time, so Umar advised learning five verses at a time.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r1.anchor: تعلموا القرآن خمس آيات خمس آيات فإن جبريل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r2.claim: He taught five verses in the morning and five in the evening, saying Gabriel brought the Qur'an in groups of five; the author qualifies this as the usual pattern, since sound reports attest both larger and smaller portions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r2.anchor: كان أبو سعيد الخدري يعلمنا القرآن خمس ءايات بالغداة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r3.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r3.claim: They add عليك after فرقناه, making the reading say that God apportioned the Qur'an to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r4.claim: على مكث means with deliberation and measured pace, making memorization easier and understanding better; another view means over a long period, gradually.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r4.anchor: أي تؤدة وتأن فإنه أيسر للحفظ وأعون على الفهم روي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r5.claim: Grammarians differ whether على مكث attaches to فرقناه or لتقرأه; it may be object plus circumstantial phrase, a circumstantial accusative, or an implied noun. Abu al-Baqa takes it as a state; al-Hawfi's proposed apposition to على الناس is rejected because مكث describes reader or recitation, not people.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r5.anchor: وفي البحر لا يبالي بتعلق هذين الحرفين بما ذكر الاختلاف معناهما لأن الأول في موضع المفعول به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r6.speaker: القراء وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r6.claim: مكث is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, not kasra; Ibn Atiyya claims consensus on ḍamma.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p188/r6.anchor: والمكث مثلث الميم وقريء بالضم والفتح ولم يقرأ بالكسر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p189/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p189/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p189/r1.claim: The Qur'an was sent down in stages according to events and benefits; this restates the gradual division while explaining its purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p189/r1.anchor: على حسب الحوادث والمصالح فذكر هذا بعد قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r6.claim: One explanation says the Qur'an was revealed in portions, supported by Ibn Abbas's intensive reading; the common light reading means it was separated or clarified.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r6.anchor: وقرآنا فرقناه} قيل: معناه: أنزلناه نجوما لم ينزل مرة واحدة بدليل قراءة ابن عباس:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the Qur'an was divided in order to distinguish truth from falsehood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه فرقنا به بين الحق والباطل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r8.claim: Revelation was recited to people gradually, calmly and with measured recitation over twenty-three years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p135#2/r8.anchor: لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} أي: على تؤدة وترتيل (2) وترسل في ثلاث

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r1.claim: One explanation is that the Qur’an was revealed in separate installments; another takes the phrase as distinguishing truth from falsehood by eliding a preposition, as in the cited expression.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r1.anchor: نزلناه مفرقا منجما. وقيل فرقنا فيه الحق من الباطل فحذف الجار

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r2.claim: A reading with a doubled consonant emphasizes its many installments, since revelation unfolded over twenty years.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r2.anchor: وقرىء بالتشديد لكثرة نجومه فإنه نزل في تضاعيف عشرين سنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r3.claim: The paced recitation gives people time, making memorization easier and understanding more attainable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r3.anchor: على مهل وتؤدة فإنه أيسر للحفظ وأعون في الفهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r4.claim: The reading with fatḥa in makth is a dialectal variant.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:106/r5.claim: Its gradual sending followed the sequence of events.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r1.claim: The Qur'an was divided and revealed in stages over time, distinct from falsehood and miraculous above all other speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r1.anchor: أنزلنا منجما في أوقات متطاولة وميزناه بالحقيقة عن كل باطل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r2.claim: It was recited to all people Muhammad could reach because his mission extends to all humanity.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r2.anchor: عامة كل من أمكنك منهم , فإنك مرسل إليهم كلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r3.claim: 'At measured pace' means reading each portion in its revealed time across twenty-three years, since people need extended periods and sustained teaching to improve.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r3.anchor: بأن تقرأ منه كل نجم في وقته الذي أنزلناه فيه مدة ثلاث وعشرين سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r4.claim: Successive revelation matched events, strengthened understanding through reflection, aided memorization, steadied Muhammad's heart, and repeatedly brought the beloved's news like a daily celebration.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p435/r4.anchor: وأعون على الفهم لطول التأمل لما نزل من نجومه في مدة ما بين النجمين

DURR-FULL:v5p344/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas's emphatic reading is linked to the Qur'an descending all at once to the lowest heaven on Ramadan's Night of Decree, then being apportioned over twenty years to answer new questions.
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن قرأ {وقرآنا فرقناه} مثقلة قال: نزل القرآن إلى سماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر

DURR-FULL:v5p344/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r9.claim: In a second account, the Qur'an descends from the Preserved Tablet to the noble scribes in the lowest heaven; they send it to Gabriel over twenty nights and Gabriel conveys it to the Prophet over twenty years.
DURR-FULL:v5p344/r9.anchor: من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: نزل القرآن جملة واحد من عند الله من اللوح المحفوظ

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r1.claim: The continuation explains that gradual descent answered the polytheists' demand for a single revelation and steadied the Prophet's heart; it allowed answers to their questions, with a link to 25:32.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r1.anchor: فقال المشركون: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحد فقال الله (كذلك لنثبت به

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r2.claim: Another report says the Qur'an descended together to the House of Might in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it to Muhammad in response to people's words and deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة حتى وضع في بيت العزة في السماء الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas's reading through Abu al-Aliya means the Qur'an was sent down verse by verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r3.anchor: من طريق أبي العالية عن ابن عباس أنه قرأها مثقلة يقول: أنزل آية آية

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r4.claim: Umar recommends learning five verses at a time because Gabriel brought the Qur'an to the Prophet in groups of five.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r4.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: تعلموا القرآن خمس آيات خمس آيات فإن جبريل كان ينزل بالقرآن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r5.claim: Abu Saeed al-Khudri taught five verses each morning and evening, saying Gabriel brought the Qur'an five verses at a time.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r5.anchor: كان أبو سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه يعلمنا القرآن خمس آيات بالغداة وخمس آيات بالعشي

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab's lighter reading makes the phrase mean that the Qur'an was clarified.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ {وقرآنا فرقناه} مخففا يعني بيناه

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Qur'an as divided into parts, at a measured period, and says falling on the chins means falling on the faces.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وقرآنا فرقناه} قال: فصلناه {على مكث} بأمد

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the measured pace as gradual or unhurried recitation.

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r9.claim: Qatada says the Qur'an was not sent down in one night, two nights, a month, two months, a year, or two years; its descent lasted twenty years or as God willed.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وقرآنا فرقناه} الآية قال: لم ينزل في ليلة ولا ليلتين ولا شهر ولا شهرين

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says revelation lasted eight years in Mecca and ten after the migration.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r10.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: كان يقال: أنزل القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p345/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r11.claim: Qatada gives ten years in Mecca and ten years in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v5p345/r11.anchor: وكان قتادة يقول: عشر بمكة وعشر بالمدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r1.claim: The verse coordinates with 17:105; “Qur'an” is an advanced circumstantial phrase for the object pronoun, praising it as a recitable book whose name comes from recitation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r2.claim: Scripture has names—Book, Qur'an, Criterion, Reminder, Sending—used according to context; only Muhammad's revealed book is styled Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r2.anchor: فهذا الكتاب له أسماء باختلاف صفاته فهو كتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r3.claim: Faraqnāhu means divided it, revealing in portions rather than one mass; it may also mean clarified and distinguished it, so the phrase means divided and made it recitable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r3.anchor: أي أنزلناه منجما مفرقا غير مجتمع صبرة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r4.claim: Its two purposes are reciting it to people and doing so slowly: the first explains its being a Qur'an, the second its piecemeal revelation, letting words and meanings settle in listeners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r4.anchor: فهما علتان : أن يقرأ على الناس وتلك علة لجعله قرآنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r5.claim: The doubled verb and cognate object in “We sent it down” signal the gradual revelation already expressed by its division.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p230#2/r5.anchor: وفي فعل { نزلناه } المضاعف وتأكيده بالمفعول المطلق إشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r1.claim: The omitted wisdom is supplied by measured recitation and 25:32: gradual revelation strengthens the Prophet's heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r1.anchor: من اتحاد الحكمة . وهي ما صرح به قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r2.claim: Alternatively, revelation was divided to accord with causes and events; both explanations answer those asking why it was not sent all at once.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p232/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : فرقنا إنزاله رعيا للأسباب والحوادث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh parses qurʾānan as governed by an omitted verb explained by the next: “We divided a Qur'an.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r4.anchor: مذهب سيبويه أن نصبه بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, qurʾānan can be coordinated with pronoun in arsalanāka because sending and revealing serve one purpose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r5.anchor: ويصح أن يكون معطوفا على الكاف في أرسلناك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r6.speaker: جمهور من الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r6.claim: The majority read farraqnāhu lightly, meaning clarified, distinguished, or made a criterion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ جمهور من الناس «فرقناه» بتخفيف الراء، ومعناه بيناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو رجاء وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب والشعبي وحميد وعمرو بن فائد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r7.claim: They read farraqnāhu with doubled rāʾ; Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy add “to him,” emphasizing portions, matching measured recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو رجاء وعلي بن أبي طالب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r8.claim: Gradual revelation followed events over time; estimates are 25, 23 from Ibn ʿAbbās, 20 from Qatāda, and 18 attributed to al-Ḥasan, which is called unsound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p490#2/r8.anchor: فَقيل: في خمس وعشرين سنة، وقال ابن عباس: في ثلاث وعشرين سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r1.claim: They take “at a measured pace” to mean deliberate recitation or tartīl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r1.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج وابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r2.claim: A second interpretation is a long span, with revelation coming portion by portion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r2.anchor: والتأويل الآخر أي على مكث وتطاول في المدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r3.claim: The verbal noun tanzīlan intensifies the preceding sense; readers agree on ḍamma on mīm of makth, though Arabic has other forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p491/r3.anchor: وقوله ونزلناه تنزيلا مبالغة وتأكيد بالمصدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r1.speaker: علي وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r1.claim: Ali and several early authorities read farraqnāhu with a doubled rāʾ, unlike the majority’s lighter reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r1.anchor: قرأ علي عليه السلام وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r2.claim: For the lighter reading, al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that it means clarifying what is lawful and unlawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r2.anchor: بينا حلاله وحرامه رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the lighter reading means distinguishing truth from falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r3.anchor: فرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra takes the lighter reading to mean that the Quran was made firm and clear, as in 44:4.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r4.anchor: أحكمناه وفصلناه كقوله تعالى فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r5.claim: The doubled reading means the Quran was revealed in separate portions, not all at once.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r5.anchor: وأما المشددة فمعناها أنه أنزل متفرقا ولم ينزل جملة واحدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r6.speaker: أنس والشعبي والضحاك وقتادة وأبو رجاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r6.claim: These readers pronounce the mīm in mukthin with fatḥa, meaning the Quran is read slowly and deliberately so people can reflect on it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p96#2/r6.anchor: قرأ أنس والشعبي والضحاك وقتادة وأبو رجاء وأبان عن عاصم وابن محيصن بفتح الميم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r4.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's reading with lightening: the Quran was transferred from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then revealed to Muhammad in installments over 23 years as events occurred.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r4.anchor: ثم نزل مفرقا منجما على الوقائع إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثلاث وعشرين سنة. قاله عكرمة عن ابن عباس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads the verb with doubling, meaning the Quran was revealed verse by verse, explained clearly, so Muhammad could recite it to people gradually.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p127/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا أنه قال {فرقناه} بالتشديد، أي: أنزلناه آية آية، مبينا مفسرا

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r1.claim: The common reading has فرقناه without doubling; Ibn Abbas and Qatada double it because revelation came gradually over more than twenty years.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: فرقناه بالتخفيف، وعن ابن عباس وقتادة بالتشديد، قال: لأنه لم ينزل مرة واحدة وإنما نزل نجوما في عشرين سنة وزيادة.

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r2.claim: Farq means separating and distinguishing parts, like parting hair.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r2.anchor: فرقناه: فصلناه كفرق الشعر، وهو تميز بعضه من بعض،

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r3.claim: Makkth means a pause or interval; all three vowel patterns on mīm are linguistic variants.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r3.anchor: والمكث: المهل وتتعاقب الحركات الثلاث عن الميم، وكلها لغات.

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r6.claim: One parsing supplies an omitted verb: We gave you a Qur’an which We divided.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r6.anchor: نصب قرآنا قيل: بمحذوف أي: وآتيناك قرآنا فرقناه.

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r7.claim: Another parsing makes فرقناه an adjective or predicate after Qur’an is placed first.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r7.anchor: ف فرقناه صفة، وقيل: فرقناه قرآنا، وفرقناه خبر على هذا،

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r8.claim: Abu Muslim allows Qur’an to coordinate with the syntactic position of وبالحق نزل, a circumstantial accusative.
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو عطف على محل قوله: وبالحق نزل فإن محله محل النصب على الحال، عن أبي مسلم،

JISHUMI:v6p4326/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4326/r9.claim: A further parsing makes قرآنا accusative under أنزلناه.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r1.claim: Qurʾānan is governed by an implied verb explained by farraqnāhu; the light reading signifies close, gradual separation, while the doubled reading means revelation came in installments.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r1.anchor: وقرءانا } منصوب بفعل يفسره { فرقناه } وقرأ أبي ( فرقناه ) بالتشديد ، أي : جعلنا نزوله مفرقا منجما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads the doubled form and says the revelation spanned twenty years, not just two or three days.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ مشددا وقال : لم ينزل في يومين أو ثلاثة ، بل كان بين أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r3.claim: Mukth is read with either fatḥa or ḍamma and means reading at leisure, deliberately, and steadily.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r3.anchor: على مكث } بالفتح والضم : على مهل وتؤدة وتثبت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p653#2/r4.claim: The Qur'an was sent down in installments in response to unfolding events.

FARRA:v2p131/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p131/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p131/r11.claim: وقرآنا is accusative either as a second description of what the Prophet was sent with, or as the object of فرقناه, resumed by its pronoun after the conjunction.
FARRA:v2p131/r11.anchor: نصبت القرآن بأرسلناك أي ما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا وقرآنا أيضا

FARRA:v2p131/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p131/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p131/r12.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s companions read فرقناه lightly, meaning “We made it firm and distinct”; Ibn ʿAbbās explains that it was not sent all at once.
FARRA:v2p131/r12.anchor: وأما (فرقناه) بالتخفيف فقد قرأه أصحاب عبد الله.

FARRA:v2p131/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p131/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p131/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an was not sent down in one day or two.
FARRA:v2p131/r13.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس (فرقناه يقول: لم ينزل في يوم ولا يومين.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r6.claim: The Quran was divided to distinguish truth from falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r6.anchor: أحدها : فرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas’s doubled-form reading means the Quran was revealed in separate verses, one at a time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r7.anchor: الثاني : فرقناه بالتشديد وهي قراءة ابن عباس أي نزل مفرقا آية آية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r8.claim: The reading “فرقناه عليك” is also found in the codices of Ibn Masud and Ubayy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r8.anchor: وهي كذلك في مصحف ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب : فرقناه عليك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r9.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r9.claim: Alternatively, the Quran was set out in distinct surahs and verses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r9.anchor: الثالث : فصلناه سورا وآيات متميزة , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r10.claim: Reading it at measured intervals means reciting deliberately and unhurriedly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r10.anchor: أحدها : يعني على تثبت وترسل , وهو قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r11.claim: Alternatively, one passage would descend, then a period would pass before another descended.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r11.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان ينزل منه شيء , ثم يمكثون بعد ما شاء الله , ثم ينزل شيء آخر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r12.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet recited it to them in portions, one after another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p279/r12.anchor: الثالث : أن يمكث في قراءته عليهم مفرقا شيئا بعد شيء , قاله أبو مسلم .

MUJAHID:v1p371#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p371#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p371#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains reciting the Qur'an at measured pace as reciting with tartil.
MUJAHID:v1p371#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ﴾ يعني في ترتيل

MUQATIL:17:105-106/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:105-106/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:105-106/r2.claim: God divided the Qur'an into portions over twenty years, not all at once, so it could be recited at a measured pace in installments.
MUQATIL:17:105-106/r2.anchor: يعني قطعناه، يعني فرقناه بين أوله وآخره، عشرون سنة تترى، لم ننزله جملة واحدة، مثلها في الفرقان:

NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r1.claim: Qurʾānan is accusative under an implied verb explained by farraqnāhu, which means either We divided it into parts or distinguished truth from falsehood within it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r1.anchor: ﴿ وقرآنا ﴾ منصوب بفعل يفسره ﴿ فرقناه ﴾ أي فصلناه أو فرقنا فيه الحق من الباطل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r2.claim: The Prophet recites it to people with deliberation and steadiness; its successive revelation followed unfolding events.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p303/r2.anchor: ﴿ لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ﴾ على تؤده وتثبت ﴿ ونزلناه تنزيلا ﴾ على حسب الحوداث

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r1.claim: Sibawayh analyzes Quranan as an accusative governed by an implied verb explained by the following verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r1.anchor: مذهب سيبويه أن «قرآنا» منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r2.speaker: جمهور الناس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r2.claim: The common light reading of farraqnahu means the Quran was clarified and truth distinguished from falsehood; Hasan gives this explanation and Ibn Abbas says it was divided into parts.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r2.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «فرقناه» بتخفيف الراء، ومعناه بيناه وأوضحناه،

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r3.claim: Hasan glosses the Quran's separation as distinguishing truth from falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r3.anchor: وفرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل قاله الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the light reading as dividing or detailing the Quran.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وقتادة وأبو رجاء والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r5.claim: These authorities read the verb with a doubled r, meaning revelation came piece by piece rather than all at once; Ibn Masud and Ubay add 'to you.'
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعلي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وقتادة وأبو رجاء والشعبي «فرقناه» بالتشديد،

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r6.claim: The reported descent period varies: Ibn Abbas says twenty-three years, Anas twenty, and another view twenty-five, reflecting disagreement about the Prophet's age; all agree it first descended to the lowest heaven at once.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r6.anchor: فقيل: في خمس وعشرين سنة. ابن عباس: في ثلاث وعشرين. أنس: في عشرين.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r7.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r7.claim: They interpret 'at a measured pace' as reciting without haste, giving each passage its due through measured, beautiful recitation without melody that alters the text; such alteration is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r7.anchor: على ترسل في التلاوة وترتيل قاله مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r8.claim: On the gradual-revelation reading, 'at a measured pace' means it came verse by verse and sura by sura; if all obligations arrived together, people would recoil.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r8.anchor: أي أنزلناه نجما بعد نجم ولو أخذوا بجميع الفرائض في وقت واحد لنفروا

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r9.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r9.claim: All readers except Ibn Muhaysin use a damma on the mīm of makth; he reads it with fatḥa, and three language forms are noted.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r9.anchor: وأجمع القراء على ضم الميم من «مكث» إلا ابن محيصن فإنه قرأ «مكث» بفتح الميم.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r10.claim: Malik glosses 'at a measured pace' as deliberate, unhurried recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:106/r10.anchor: قال مالك: «على مكث» على تثبت وترسل.

RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r1.claim: The objection says a miraculous Quran should have descended all at once, since gradual delivery makes it seem that the Messenger composed it passage by passage; gradual revelation eases memorization and understanding its details.
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r1.anchor: أن القوم قالوا : هب إن هذا القرآن معجز إلا أنه بتقدير أن يكون الأمر كذلك فكان من الواجب أن ينزله الله عليك دفعة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the whole Quran descended on the Night of Power from the highest heaven to the lowest, then was apportioned over the years.
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جيبر نزل القرآن كله ليلة القدر من السماء العليا إلى السماء السفلى ، ثم فصل في السنين

RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r3.claim: Qatada says twenty years separated the beginning of Quranic revelation from its end.
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r3.anchor: قال قتادة : كان بين أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r4.claim: The Quran was divided verse by verse and sura by sura so people could recite it slowly, calmly, and deliberately rather than in haste.
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r4.anchor: والمعنى قطعناه آية آية وسورة سورة ولم ننزله جملة لتقرأه على الناس على مكث بالفتح والضم على مهل وتؤدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r5.claim: Al-Farra records both vowelings of makth as forms of the verb meaning to remain, citing another Quranic occurrence.
RAZI-FULL:v21p57/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : يقال مكث ومكث يمكث ، والفتح قراءة عاصم في قوله : { فمكث غير بعيد } ( النمل : 22 )

RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r1.speaker: الأئمة
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r1.claim: The leading reciters prefer the light form farraqnāhu, which Abu ʿAmr interprets as making the Quran clear; Abu ʿUbayd prefers it because division implies clarification.
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r1.anchor: البحث الثالثة : الاختيار عند الأئمة فرقناه بالتخفيف وفسره أبو عمرو بيناه قال أبو عبيد : التخفيف أعجب إلي

RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r2.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r2.claim: Thaʿlab transmits Ibn al-Aʿrabi's distinction between separating speech and separating bodies as linguistic support for the light reading.
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r2.anchor: ويؤكده ما روى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي أنه قال : فرقت أفرق بين الكلام وفرقت بين الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r3.claim: The Prophetic saying about buyers' option until they separate supports the distinction: tafarruq follows tafrīq, while iftirāq follows farq.
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r3.anchor: ويدل عليه أيضا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( البيعان بالخيار ما لم يتفرقا ) ولم يقل يفترقا والتفرق مطاوع التفريق

RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r4.claim: The Quran's further sending down followed the stated manner and quality of gradual, measured revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p58/r4.anchor: ثم قال : { ونزلناه تنزيلا } أي على الحد المذكور والصفة المذكورة

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r1.speaker: JJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r1.claim: Dividing the Quran into parts refers to gradual revelation to Muhammad, allowing him to recite it at intervals.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r1.anchor: the successive and gradual revelation of the Quranic verses to the Prophet (JJ,Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r2.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r2.claim: Some say the entire Quran descended to the lower heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was revealed to Muhammad over twenty-three years.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r2.anchor: the Quran was sent down as a whole to the lower heavens in a single night (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r3.claim: Some understand the whole Quran to have entered the Prophet’s heart on that night and then been gradually revealed to his consciousness.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r3.anchor: The Quran is also understood by some as having been sent down as a whole into the very heart of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r4.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r4.claim: The Quran’s division can also mean its organization into verses or surahs of unequal length.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r4.anchor: the division of the Quran into distinct sections (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r5.speaker: Bḍ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r5.claim: Discrete revelation gave people time to learn, memorize, and understand the Quran properly.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r5.anchor: so that they would have time to learn it properly, memorize it, and come to understand it (Bḍ, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:17:106/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r6.claim: Gradual revelation also made Muhammad’s heart firm, and the text affirms that gradual descent was divinely intended.
STUDYQURAN:17:106/r6.anchor: It is so, that We may make firm thine heart thereby. And We have recited it unto thee in a measured pace

NAHHAS:v2p443/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p443/r5.claim: قرآنا is an accusative governed by an omitted verb, and فرقناه means ‘we made it clear.’
NAHHAS:v2p443/r5.anchor: نصب على اضمار فعل ^ ( فرقناه ) ^ بيناه

NAHHAS:v2p443/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p443/r6.claim: Another explanation says the Qur’an was sent piecemeal, containing warning, promise, commands, prohibitions, and accounts of past and future events.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r6.anchor: وقيل : أنزلناه متفرقا وعيدا ووعدا وأمرا ونهيا وخبرا عما كان ويكون

NAHHAS:v2p443/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
NAHHAS:v2p443/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ interprets فرقناه as ‘sent it down as a furqān,’ distinguishing truth from falsehood and believer from unbeliever.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r7.anchor: وقد اشتق مثل هذا أبو عمرو بن العلاء رحمه الله فقال : ' فرقناه ' أنزلنا فرقانا

NAHHAS:v2p443/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، الشعبي، عكرمة، قتادة
NAHHAS:v2p443/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrima, and Qatāda read فرقناه with a doubled rāʾ; it can have the same sense with added emphasis, force, and frequency.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والشعبي وعكرمة وقتادة ^ ( وقرآنا فرقناه ) ^ بالتشديد

NAHHAS:v2p443/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p443/r9.claim: على مكث means the audience could memorize and understand the recitation; the word has three cited vocal forms.
NAHHAS:v2p443/r9.anchor: أي ليحفظوه ويفهموه يقال : مكث ومكث ومكث

NAHHAS:v2p443/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p443/r10.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p443/r10.claim: Mujāhid glosses على مكث as reciting deliberately and slowly.

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r2.speaker: عامة قراء الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r2.claim: Most readers read فرقناه with a light rāʾ, meaning the Quran was made precise, distinguished, and clear.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r2.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء الأمصار {فرقناه} [الإسراء: 106] بتخفيف الراء من فرقناه

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r3.claim: A reported reading by Ibn Abbas has a doubled rāʾ and means the Quran came down successively, verse by verse and story by story.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r3.anchor: وذكر عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يقرؤه بتشديد الراء «فرقناه» بمعنى: نزلناه شيئا بعد شيء، آية بعد آية

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the light-rāʾ reading because it is the reading accepted by the community of authoritative readers and may not be opposed in Quranic matters.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r4.anchor: وأولى القراءتين بالصواب عندنا، القراءة الأولى، لأنها القراءة التي عليها الحجة مجمعة

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r5.claim: The Quran was distinguished, explained, and made precise so the Prophet could recite it to people at a measured pace.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r5.anchor: وفصلناه قرآنا، وبيناه وأحكمناه، لتقرأه على الناس على مكث

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the light-rāʾ reading as making the Quran distinct and setting matters apart.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r6.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وقرآنا فرقناه} [الإسراء: 106] يقول: فصلناه

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r7.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read the word with a light rāʾ and glossed it as making the Quran clear.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r7.anchor: عن أبي الربيع، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، أنه قرأ: {وقرآنا فرقناه} [الإسراء: 106] مخففا: يعني بيناه

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r8.claim: Al-Hasan read the form lightly, explaining that God distinguishes truth from falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r8.anchor: عن الحسن، أنه قرأ: {وقرآنا فرقناه} [الإسراء: 106] خففها: فرق الله بين الحق والباطل

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r9.claim: In the doubled-rāʾ reading, Ibn Abbas says the Quran was sent down one verse at a time.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r9.anchor: كان ابن عباس يقرؤها: «وقرآنا فرقناه» مثقلة، يقول: أنزل آية آية

TAB-FULL:v15p114/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Quran first descended whole to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr and was then revealed over twenty years.
TAB-FULL:v15p114/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة إلى السماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر، ثم أنزل بعد ذلك في عشرين سنة

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r1.claim: Qatada says the Quran was not revealed all at once; roughly twenty years separated its first and last revelation.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: «وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس» لم ينزل جميعا، وكان بين أوله وآخره نحو من عشرين سنة

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd explains فرقناه as revealing the Quran in parts, citing the disbelievers’ demand that it be sent down all at once.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: «وقرآنا فرقناه» قال: فرقه: لم ينزله جميعه

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r3.claim: A Kufan grammarian parses Qurʾānan as an accusative meaning mercy, attached to the Prophet’s being sent as bearer of good news and warning.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يقول: نصب قوله {وقرآنا} [الإسراء: 106] بمعنى: ورحمة

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers his own accusative construction for Qurʾānan to the Kufan reading, analogizing it to the moon passage.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r4.anchor: ونصبه على الوجه الذي قلناه أولى، وذلك كما قال جل ثناؤه: {والقمر قدرناه منازل}

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r5.claim: On measured pace means reciting deliberately, articulating clearly, and not rushing so listeners can understand.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r5.anchor: على تؤدة، فترتله وتبينه، ولا تعجل في تلاوته، فلا يفهم عنك

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r6.claim: When two people recite equally in bowing and prostration, Mujahid prefers the one who recites only al-Baqara, citing measured recitation.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r6.anchor: قلت لمجاهد: رجل قرأ البقرة وآل عمران، وآخر قرأ البقرة، وركوعهما وسجودهما واحد

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses على مكث as reading with continued steadiness or deliberation.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r7.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} [الإسراء: 106] يقول: على تأييد

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets the phrase as recitation with tartil.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {على مكث} [الإسراء: 106] قال: على ترتيل

TAB-FULL:v15p116/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj likewise says the Quran should be read with tartil.
TAB-FULL:v15p116/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} [الإسراء: 106] قال: في ترتيل

TAB-FULL:v15p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd connects measured recitation with the command to recite the Quran in tartil, meaning explained recitation.
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} [الإسراء: 106] قال: التفسير الذي قال الله {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا } [المزمل: 4] تفسيره

TAB-FULL:v15p118/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses على مكث as reading with deliberation or unhurried ease.
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} [الإسراء: 106] على تؤدة

TAB-FULL:v15p118/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r3.claim: Arabic uses several forms for the word مكث, while the canonical reading has ḍamma on the mīm.
TAB-FULL:v15p118/r3.anchor: وفي المكث للعرب لغات: مكث، ومكث، ومكث ومكيثي مقصور، ومكثانا، والقراءة بضم الميم

TAB-FULL:v15p119/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Quran was revealed in stages as God knew events would arise among people; he places the period at eighteen years, eight in Mecca and ten in Medina.
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r1.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، قال: تلا الحسن: «وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا» قال: كان الله تبارك وتعالى ينزل هذا القرآن بعضه قبل بعض

TAB-FULL:v15p119/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r2.claim: Al-Hasan corrects Abu Raja’s doubled-rāʾ reading, insisting on the light-rāʾ form, and says the report comes from the Prophet’s Companions.
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r2.anchor: فثقلها أبو رجاء، فقال الحسن: ليس فرقناه، ولكن فرقناه، فقرأ الحسن مخففة

TAB-FULL:v15p119/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r3.claim: Qatada says revelation took much longer than one night, month, or year: twenty years separated its beginning and end, or as God willed.
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا} [الإسراء: 106] لم ينزل في ليلة ولا ليلتين

TAB-FULL:v15p119/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r4.claim: Al-Hasan also places revelation over eight years before the Hijra and ten years afterward.
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: كان يقول: أنزل على نبي الله القرآن ثماني سنين، وعشرا بعد ما هاجر

TAB-FULL:v15p119/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r5.claim: Qatada instead gives ten years in Mecca and ten in Medina.
TAB-FULL:v15p119/r5.anchor: وكان قتادة يقول: عشرا بمكة، وعشرا بالمدينة

TABATABAI:17:105-107/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r1.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r1.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses farraqnāhu as dividing or detailing the Qurʾān, sending it down verse by verse and sūrah by sūrah; mukth has both u-vowel and a-vowel pronunciations.
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r1.anchor: قال في المجمع معنى فرقناه فصلناه ونزلناه آية آية وسورة سورة ويدل عليه قوله { على مكث }

TABATABAI:17:105-107/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r2.claim: The wording also covers rendering the unified divine truths into Arabic expressions that people can receive gradually, making the message easier to understand and memorize.
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r2.anchor: التي هي عند الله في قالب الألفاظ والعبارات التي لا تتلقى إلا بالتدريج

TABATABAI:17:105-107/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r3.claim: The second sense of division, gradual descent, entails ordering diverse teachings and rulings out of one unified source; revelation came in stages over twenty-three years to pair instruction with practice and suit people's capacities.
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r3.anchor: في تمام ثلاث وعشرين سنة ليشفع التعليم بالتربية ويقرن العلم بالعمل

TABATABAI:17:105-107/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r4.claim: Given the surrounding demand for a book to read all at once, he prefers that the verse mean revelation in separate sūrahs and verses as occasions arose; unbelievers and People of the Book had likewise asked for a complete book at once.
TABATABAI:17:105-107/r4.anchor: هو أن يكون المراد بتفريق القرآن إنزاله سورة سورة وآية آية حسب تحقق أسباب النزول تدريجا

TABATABAI:17:111#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r8.claim: The Qurʾān itself repeatedly recognizes the sūrah and verse as its constituent units, and a sūrah is a basmala-prefaced group of divine speech organized around a purpose, with reported exceptions in counting.
TABATABAI:17:111#3/r8.anchor: فقد كرر الله سبحانه ذكرهما في كلامه كقوله

TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r1.claim: An ayah is a naturally distinct unit that can be recited separately; units vary from one word to several phrases or a very long passage, especially with rhythmic contexts.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r1.anchor: أن الآية من القرآن هي قطعة من الكلام من حقها أن تعتمد عليها التلاوة بفصلها عما قبلها وعما بعدها

TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r2.claim: Reports say the Prophet paused at the ends of verses; the recitation tradition also counts al-Fātiḥah as seven verses and al-Mulk as thirty, supporting the existence of verse units.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#3/r2.anchor: وقد روي عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يقف على رؤوس الآي

TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r1.claim: The familiar Uthmanic codex has 114 sūrahs, while the Ahl al-Bayt do not count Barāʾa separately and combine al-Ḍuḥā with al-Inshirāḥ and al-Fīl with Quraysh.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r1.anchor: فهي مائة وأربع عشره سورة على ما جرى عليه الرسم في المصحف الدائر بيننا

TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r2.claim: No reliable mutawātir text fixes verse boundaries; the regional counting traditions disagree both on total verses and endpoints, so where boundaries are not obvious a researcher may judge from the evidence.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r2.anchor: فقد قال بعضهم أن مجموع القرآن ستة آلاف آية، وقال بعضهم ستة آلاف ومأتان وأربع آيات

TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r3.claim: The regional counts trace to different transmitters: Meccan counts through Ibn Kathīr, Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ubayy; two Medinan traditions; Abū al-Dardāʾ for Syria; al-Jaḥdarī for Basra; and Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf for Kufa.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#4/r3.anchor: وقد روى المكيون عددهم عن عبد الله بن كثير عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب

TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r1.claim: The Kufan count attributed to ʿAlī conflicts with reports that the basmala is a Qurʾanic verse in every sūrah that opens with it; the author therefore omits detailed disputed counts and refers readers to their sources.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r1.anchor: والذي روي عن علي عليه السلام من عدد الكوفيين معارض بأن البسملة غير معدودة في شيء من السور

TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r2.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās gives the descending order of revelation, beginning with Read in the name of your Lord, then Nūn, al-Muzzammil, and al-Muddaththir, and continues through the Meccan sūrahs.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#5/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كانت إذا نزلت فاتحة سورة بمكة كتبت بمكة ثم يزيد الله فيها ما شاء

TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r1.claim: The transmitted lists give a Medinan revelation sequence; they omit al-Fātiḥah, perhaps because it was revealed twice, and variant reports disagree over the ordering and inclusion of several sūrahs.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r1.anchor: وقد سقطت من الرواية سورة فاتحة الكتاب وربما قيل إنها نزلت مرتين مرة بمكة ومرة بالمدينة

TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r2.speaker: ابن حصار
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r2.claim: Ibn Ḥaṣṣār reports twenty sūrahs are agreed to be Medinan and twelve are disputed, with the rest agreed to be Meccan; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī lists the named categories.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r2.anchor: أن المدني باتفاق عشرون سورة، والمختلف فيه اثنا عشرة سورة وما عدا ذلك مكي باتفاق

TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r3.claim: Knowing Meccan and Medinan origins and revelation order matters for analyzing the prophetic mission, but the conflicting reports cannot establish it; careful study of contextual and internal or external clues is the sound method.
TABATABAI:17:101-111#6/r3.anchor: والروايات - كما ترى - لا تصلح أن تنهض حجة معتمدا عليها في إثبات شيء من ذلك

TABRISI:17:106-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:106-108/r1.claim: The common reading lightens farraqnāh; ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ubayy, al-Shaʿbī, al-Ḥasan with a variant, Qatāda, and ʿAmr b. Fāʾid use the doubled form, meaning divided into verses and chapters.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r1.anchor: القراءة المشهورة في فرقناه بالتخفيف وروي عن علي ع وابن مسعود

TABRISI:17:106-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:17:106-108/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains farraqnāh as separating truth from falsehood; another view divides it into reports, commands, prohibitions, promises, and warnings.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه فرقنا به الحق عن الباطل عن الحسن

TABRISI:17:106-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:17:106-108/r3.claim: Abū Muslim says God divided the Qurʾān into chapters and verses and revealed it gradually across more than twenty years.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه جعلنا بعضه خبرا وبعضه أمرا وبعضه نهيا

TABRISI:17:106-108/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:106-108/r4.claim: Gradual revelation lets the Prophet recite steadily, making the text firmer in listeners’ hearts and giving room to reflect; it follows needs and events.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r4.anchor: على تثبت وتؤدة فترتله ليكون أمكن في قلوبهم

TABRISI:17:106-108/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:17:106-108/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid explain measured pace as reciting in separate portions rather than rushing.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r5.anchor: وقيل معناه لتقرأه عليهم مفرقا شيئا بعد شيء

TABRISI:17:106-108/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:106-108/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās prefers slowly reciting Sūrat al-Baqara over reciting the entire Qurʾān quickly.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: لئن أقرأ سورة البقرة وأرتلها أحب إلي

TABRISI:17:106-108/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:106-108/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:17:106-108/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says not to recite the Qurʾān in fewer than three days and recommends seven.
TABRISI:17:106-108/r7.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال لا تقرأوا القرآن في أقل من ثلاث

THALABI:v6p140/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p140/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p140/r8.claim: The Quran was revealed as a recitation and divided into parts.
THALABI:v6p140/r8.anchor: وقرآنا فرقناه أي وأنزلناه قرآنا ففصلناه.

THALABI:v6p140/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p140/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p140/r9.claim: He reads farraqnahu with doubled rāʾ: the Quran was divided because it was not revealed all at once, but in installments over twenty years; Ubayy’s reading adds ‘upon you.’
THALABI:v6p140/r9.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس: فرقناه بالتشديد وقال: لأنه لم ينزل مرة واحدة

THALABI:v6p140/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p140/r10.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v6p140/r10.claim: Other reciters read the verb lightly, likening it to the wording that every wise matter is distinguished.
THALABI:v6p140/r10.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتخفيف كقوله فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم.

THALABI:v6p140/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p140/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
THALABI:v6p140/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as ‘explained it’; al-Hasan says God distinguished truth from falsehood through it, and other readers say ‘made it clear.’
THALABI:v6p140/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس فصلناه، قال الحسن: فرق الله به بين الحق والباطل

THALABI:v6p140/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p140/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p140/r12.claim: The gradual recitation lets people hear it at a measured, gentle pace over twenty-three years.
THALABI:v6p140/r12.anchor: لتقرأه على الناس على مكث أي تؤدة ومهل في ثلاث وعشرين سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r1.claim: Qurʾānan is accusative through an implied verb, or may be the object of anzalnāhu.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وقرآنا فرقناه} ينتصب قرآنا بإضمار فعل،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r2.claim: Alternatively, Qur'an could coordinate with 'We sent you' by deleting an annexed phrase, though this would make a proper name indefinite in an awkward way, despite 39:28.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r2.anchor: والوجه الآخر: أن تعطفه على ما يتصل به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r3.claim: He explains farraqnāhu as having separated or set out the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r3.anchor: {فرقناه}: فصلناه، قاله علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r4.claim: The whole Qur'an descended on the Night of Decree from the highest heaven to the lowest, then was sent down during the years of revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير عنه: نزل القرآن كله ليلة القدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r5.claim: Twenty years passed between the beginning and end of revelation; this is the gradual recitation denoted by 'at a measured pace.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان بين أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r6.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r6.claim: The Qur'an was divided verse by verse and surah by surah rather than sent all at once.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: قطعناه آية آية وسورة سورة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r7.speaker: الأئمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r7.claim: The preferred reading is the light form farraqnāhu; Abu ʿAmr glosses it as 'We explained it.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r7.anchor: والاختيار عند الأئمة: فرقناه مخففا (4)، وفسره أبو عمرو: بيناه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r8.claim: He glosses the light form as perfected and distinguished, as in the separation of every wise matter at 44:4.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء: أحكمناه (6) وفصلناه؛ كما قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r9.claim: The light reading means exposition, while the heavy form means only sending in separate portions; the author summarizes that farq includes clarification and tafrīq does not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r9.anchor: وحصل من هذا أن معنى الفرق تفصيل يتضمن التبيين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r10.speaker: ابن الأعرابي عن ثعلب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r10.claim: He distinguishes farraqa for separating speech from bodies; the Prophet's hadith says buyers retain the option until they separate, using tafarraqa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r10.anchor: ما روى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي أنه قال: فرقت أفرق بين الكلام،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r11.claim: ʿAlā makthin means reciting with deliberation and measured slowness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p502/r11.anchor: ومعنى: {على مكث} على تؤدة وترسل، قاله مجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r1.claim: Makath has several noun and verb forms; the fatḥa form occurs in 27:22 in ʿĀṣim's reading, and revelation came in installments for people to understand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: مكث ومكث ومكث، ويقال في الفعل:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r2.claim: God sent the Qur'an down star by star and thing after thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p504/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: [نجوما بعد نجوم، وشيئا بعد شيء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r9.claim: God divided the Qur’an into verses and surahs over twenty years.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r9.anchor: { وقرآنا فرقناه } قطعناه آية آية، وسورة سورة في عشرين سنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r10.claim: Measured, unhurried recitation lets people understand it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r10.anchor: { لتقرأه على الناس على مكث } تؤدة وترسل ليفهموه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r11.claim: Its revelation came gradually, in successive portions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:102-107/r11.anchor: { ونزلناه تنزيلا } نجوما بعد نجوم وشيئا بعد شيء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r7.claim: God revealed the Qur'an over twenty-three years so the Prophet could recite it to people gradually.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r7.anchor: أنزله الله في ثلاث وعشرين سنة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r8.claim: On the lighter reading, farraqnahu means the Qur'an distinguishes truth from falsehood and lawful from unlawful.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r8.anchor: من قرأها بالتخفيف قال: فرق فيه بين الحق والباطل والحلال والحرام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r9.speaker: الحسن بن دينار
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r9.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Dinar read the verb with emphasis: God divided the Qur'an, revealing it day by day, month by month, and year by year until its intended completion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r9.anchor: الحسن بن دينار، أنه كان يقرأها مثقلة فرقناه. قال: فرقه الله؛ فأنزله يوما بعد يوم، وشهرا بعد شهر، وعاما بعد عام،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r10.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r10.claim: Mujahid glosses على مكث as reciting deliberately and measuredly among Quraysh.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مكث: على ترسل في قريش.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r11.claim: The Qur'an descended all at once to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then came down in portions of three, four, five, or other numbers of verses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p166/r11.anchor: همام، عن الكلبي، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، قال: نزل القرآن إلى السماء الدنيا جملة واحدة ليلة القدر، ثم جعل بعد ذلك ينزل نجوما: ثلاث آيات، وأربع وخمس آيات وأقل من ذلك وأكثر.

ELMALILI:17:106/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:106/r1.claim: The Quran was divided into portions so the Prophet could recite it slowly and at intervals.
ELMALILI:17:106/r1.anchor: ağır ağır, vakit vakit nâsa kıraat edesin için Biz onu ayırt

ELMALILI:17:106/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:106/r2.claim: Its revelation was gradual, from foundational principles toward subsidiary matters, matching people's needs and circumstances rather than arriving all at once.
ELMALILI:17:106/r2.anchor: hepsini birden değil, usûlden fürû‘a doğru nâsın her türlü mesâlih ve ihtiyâcâtına ve ahvâlin muktezayâtına mutabık olmak üzere tedrîcen indirdik.

ELMALILI:17:106/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:106/r3.claim: Even a section, a tenth, or sometimes a single verse can stand as a complete lesson containing glad tidings and warning.
ELMALILI:17:106/r3.anchor: bir hizib veya bir aşır ve hatta bazen bir âyet müstakil bir kitap gibi başlı başına tebşir ve inzârı muhtevî bir derstir.

ELMALILI:17:106/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r4.speaker: Ömer
ELMALILI:17:106/r4.claim: A report attributed to Umar says to learn the Quran five verses at a time because Gabriel revealed it in fives.
ELMALILI:17:106/r4.anchor: Ömer radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle dediğini tahric etmiştir: ‘Kur’ân’ı beşer âyet beşer âyet ta‘allüm ediniz.

ELMALILI:17:106/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r5.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî
ELMALILI:17:106/r5.claim: Abu Sa'id reportedly taught five verses morning and evening and said Gabriel revealed the Quran in groups of five.
ELMALILI:17:106/r5.anchor: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî bize Kur’ân’ı sabah beş ve akşam beş âyet tâlim eder

ELMALILI:17:106/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:106/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:106/r6.claim: Although sound evidence establishes revelations of more and fewer than five verses, the reports mean that five-at-a-time was usual.
ELMALILI:17:106/r6.anchor: beşten daha fazla ve daha az olarak nüzûlünün vâki‘olduğu da sahîhen sâbit bulunduğundan murad, ekseriya demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r4.claim: Revelation in portions over nearly twenty-three years let the Prophet convey divine messages gradually, explaining and adapting them to people's circumstances so they could absorb them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r4.anchor: âyetler ve sûreler halinde kısım kısım indirilmiş; bu da Resûlullah’ın ilâhî tebliğleri insanlara zamana, zemine ihtiyaçlara ve şartlara göre yavaş yavaş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r5.claim: Gradual revelation helped believers adopt rulings step by step and made it easier to leave entrenched habits and beliefs, as with the wine prohibition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:105/r5.anchor: içki yasağıyla ilgili âyetlerde olduğu gibi bazı âyetler, insanların doğal olarak birden terketmeleri mümkün olmayan kötü alışkanlıklarını, yanlış inanç ve telakkilerini zaman içinde terketmelerini kolaylaştıracak bir süreçte indirilmiştir.

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r1.claim: One parse supplies an implicit verb, “We gave you a Qurʾan,” supported by the earlier mention of God's giving Moses signs.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه منصوب بفعل مقدر، أي: وآتيناك قرآنا

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya coordinates qurʾānan with the pronoun in arsalnāka because sending the Messenger and sending the Qurʾan convey one meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " من حيث كان إرسال هذا وإنزال هذا معنى واحدا

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ coordinates Qurʾan with mubashshiran and nadhīran under arsalnāka, construing the Qurʾan itself as mercy.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: هو منصوب ب " أرسلناك " ، أي: ما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا وقرآنا، كما تقول: ورحمة لأن القرآن رحمة

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r4.claim: The author says this coordination is strained; positing an omitted word meaning bearer of a Qurʾan is more plausible.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r4.anchor: قلت: يعني أنه جعل نفس القرآن مرادا به الرحمة مبالغة، ولو ادعى ذلك على حذف مضاف كان أقرب

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r5.claim: A fourth parse uses اشتغال: an implicit farraqnā is repeated, and a deleted qualifier licenses the construction; farraqnāhu then has no syntactic case.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r5.anchor: الرابع: أن ينتصب على الاشتغال، أي: وفرقنا قرآنا فرقناه. واعتذر الشيخ عن ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r6.claim: Under the اشتغال parse, farraqnāhu has no syntactic case; under the other parses it is an accusative adjective of qurʾānan.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r6.anchor: و " فرقناه " على هذا لا محل له بخلاف الأوجه المتقدمة؛ فإن محله النصب لأنه نعت ل " قرآنا "

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r7.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r7.claim: The common ungeminated reading means explaining lawful and forbidden matters or distinguishing truth from falsehood.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r7.anchor: والعامة " فرقناه " بالتخفيف، أي: بينا حلاله وحرامه، أو فرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r8.speaker: علي وأبي وعبد الله وابن عباس والشعبي وقتادة وحميد
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r8.claim: Ali, Ubayy, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, Qatada, Humayd, and others read the verb with gemination.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r8.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب - كرم الله وجهه - وابي وعبد الله وابن عباس والشعبي وقتادة وحميد في آخرين بالتشديد

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r9.claim: With gemination, one explanation is intensive division into commands, rulings, admonitions, parables, stories, and past and future reports; another is successive sending.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r9.anchor: أحدهما: أن التضعيف فيه للتكثير، أي: فرقنا آياته بين أمر ونهي وحكم وأحكام ومواعظ وأمثال

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attributes to Ibn ʿAbbas a geminated reading and the statement that revelation spanned twenty years.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وعن ابن عباس أنه قرأ مشددا، وقال: لم ينزل في يومين ولا في ثلاثة

SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r11.claim: The author says the gradual-revelation view is not clearly transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas: the shaykh separates the general view from his twenty-year statement.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106/r11.anchor: قلت: وظاهر/ هذا أن القول بالتنجيم ليس مرويا عن ابن عباس ولا سيما وقد فصل قوله

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r1.anchor: قوله: " لتقرأه " متعلق ب " فرقناه ". و " على مكث "

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r2.claim: One parse treats ʿalā makthin as an implicit circumstance for the reader or recited text, meaning slowly and deliberately.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r2.anchor: أحدها: أنه متعلق بمحذوف، على أنه حال من الفاعل أو المفعول في

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r3.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi makes ʿalā makthin an apposition to ʿalā al-nās; the author calls this mistaken because it describes the reader or recitation, not the people.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه بدل من " على الناس " قاله الحوفي، وهو وهم، لأن قوله

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r4.claim: A third parse attaches ʿalā makthin directly to farraqnāhu.

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r5.claim: The shaykh prefers attaching ʿalā makthin to li-taqraʾahu, taking it as a circumstance despite the repeated preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r5.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " والظاهر تعلق " على مكث " بقوله " لتقرأه " ، ولا يبالى بكون الفعل يتعلق به حرفا جر

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r6.claim: The author says the shaykh's syntactic explanation conflicts with calling it a circumstance, which must attach to an implicit governor.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r6.anchor: قلت: قوله أولا إنه متعلق بقوله " لتقرأه " ينافي قوله في موضع الحال؛ لأنه متى كان حالا تعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r7.claim: Makth means a long duration; three vowel patterns exist, but the author knows readings only with ḍamma and fatḥa, not kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:17:106#2/r7.anchor: والمكث: التطاول في المدة وفيه ثلاثة لغات: الضم والفتح - ونقل القراءة بهما الحوفي وأبو البقاء - والكسر

ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r4.claim: Qurʾānan faraqnāhu is also read with a doubled rāʾ, farraqnāhu.
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r4.anchor: وتقرأ (فرقناه) - بالتشديد، وقرآنا منصوب بفعل مضمر،

ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r5.claim: Qurʾānan is accusative through an implied verb, continuing the statement that the Prophet was sent to give glad tidings and warnings.
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r5.anchor:
وقرآنا منصوب بفعل مضمر،
المعنى: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا، تبشر المؤمنين بالجنة وتنذر من عصى الله بالنار، وقرآنا فرقناه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r6.claim: The Qur’an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven, then revealed to the Prophet over twenty years and divided so people could understand it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r6.anchor:
القرآن جملة واحدة إلى سماء الدنيا، ثم أنزل على
النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في عشرين سنة، فرقه الله في التنزيل ليفهمه الناس

ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r7.claim: Mكث means measured intervals; the word is read with a ḍamma on the mīm.
ZAJJAJ:v3p263/r7.anchor:
فقال: (لتقرأه على الناس على مكث).
ومكث جميعا، والقراءة بضم الميم.

ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r1.claim: The verb can literally mean that the Qur'an was divided into consecutive parts.
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r1.anchor: which We have divided into [consecutive] parts

ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r2.speaker: some authorities quoted by Razi
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r2.claim: Some authorities quoted by Razi read the verb as setting the Qur'an forth with clarity.
