ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r2.anchor: according to some authorities (quoted by Razi), "set forth with clarity"

ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r3.claim: Asad's chosen rendering is meant to preserve both senses.
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n128/r3.anchor: The rendering adopted by me allows for both these meanings.

ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r1.claim: The Qur'an's revelation unfolded gradually over the Prophet's 23-year ministry.
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r1.anchor: the process of the revelation of the Qur'an was gradual, extending over the twenty-three years of the Prophet's ministry

ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r2.claim: Although revealed gradually, the Qur'an is one whole and each passage should be read in light of all the others.
ASAD-NOTES:17:105#n129/r2.anchor: it is nevertheless one integral whole and can, therefore, be properly understood only if it is considered in its entirety

QIRAAT-ER:17:106:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:106:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:106:2#1/r1.claim: Dropping hamza yields qurānan without a glottal stop, simplifying pronunciation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:17:106:2#1/r1.anchor: Canonical seven reading: hamza dropped, producing qurānan without glottal stop

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Qurʾān was revealed in portions rather than all at once, over roughly twenty years.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وقرآنا فرقناه ﴾ قال نزل متفرقا ولم ينزل جمعا كان بين أوله وآخره نحو من عشرين سنة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses reading it ʿalā makth as reading it slowly and deliberately.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ﴾ قال على تؤدة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid says its sending down in stages means one part followed by another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r3.anchor: أخبرني الثوري أيضا قال أخبرني منصور عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ونزلناه تنزيلا ﴾ قال بعضه على أثر بعض

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r4.speaker: عطاء
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ distinguishes casting something away from the measured recitation implied by tartīl.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r4.anchor: قلت لعطاء ما قوله ﴿ ورتلناه ترتيلا ﴾ قال الطرح هو النبذ فإذا هو لا يوجب الترتيل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r5.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r5.claim: Ṭāwūs says tartīl means making the recitation clear so that it can be understood.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p391#3/r5.anchor: عن أبيه قال الترتيل تبينه حتى تفهمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r21.claim: مكث means an extended duration or a long stay; both vocalized forms are used.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p95/r21.anchor: المكث: التطاول في المدة، يقال: مكث ومكث أطال الإقامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r8.claim: On the majority's light-r reading فرقناه, Ibn Abbas says the Quran clarifies what is lawful and unlawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فرقناه بتخفيف الراء أي بينا حلاله وحرامه قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the Quran distinguishes truth from falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r9.anchor: وعن الحسن فرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r10.claim: Al-Farra glosses فرقناه as making the Quran firm and clearly delineated, like the division of every wise affair.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p122/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: أحكمناه وفصلناه كقوله فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r1.speaker: أبي وعبد الله وعلي وابن عباس وأبو رجاء وقتادة والشعبي وحميد وعمرو بن قائد وزيد بن علي وعمرو بن ذر وعكرمة والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r1.claim: They read فرقناه with a doubled r: God sent the Quran down successively, in separate portions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله وعلي وابن عباس وأبو رجاء وقتادة والشعبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r2.claim: Some advocates of the doubled-r reading say revelation was not sent in one or two days, months, or years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r2.anchor: وقال بعض من اختار ذلك: لم ينزل في يوم ولا يومين ولا شهر ولا شهرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported as giving twenty years between the beginning and end of revelation; other reports give twenty-three or twenty-five years, tied to differing accounts of the Prophet's age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان بين أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r4.claim: Al-Hasan is reported as saying revelation lasted eighteen years, but Ibn Atiyya says this report from him is unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن نزل في ثمانية عشر سنة. قال ابن عطية: وهذا قول مختل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r5.claim: Another explanation of the doubled-r form is that the Quran's verses are divided into commands, rulings, admonitions, parables, narratives, and reports of unseen events.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r5.anchor: وقيل معنى: فرقناه بالتشديد فرقنا آياته بين أمر ونهي، وحكم وأحكام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r6.claim: قرآنا is preferably accusative by an implied verb explained by فرقناه; this coordinates with the preceding verbal clause, though an adjective is supplied for its indefinite form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r6.anchor: وانتصب قرآنا على إضمار فعل يفسره فرقناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r7.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r7.claim: Al-Farra makes قرآنا an object of أرسلناك, because the Quran is a mercy; the author calls this parsing strained.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r8.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r8.claim: They add عليك, reading فرقناه عليك.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله فرقناه عليك بزيادة عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r9.claim: لتقرأه attaches to فرقناه; على مكث attaches to the reading as a state, meaning measured and unhurried, despite both prepositions being alike.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p123/r9.anchor: والظاهر تعلق على مكث بقوله لتقرأه ولا يبالى بكون الفعل يتعلق به حرفا جر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r1.claim: They gloss على مكث as deliberate, measured recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جريج: على مكث على ترسل في التلاوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r2.claim: Another gloss takes على مكث as a long span, with revelation given little by little.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r2.anchor: وقيل: على مكث أي تطاول في المدة شيئا بعد شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi makes على مكث a substitute for على الناس; the author rejects this because measured pace describes the Messenger or recitation, not the people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي: على مكث بدل من على الناس وهذا لا يصح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says all readers agree on damma in the mīm of مكث.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وأجمع القراء على ضم الميم من مكث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r5.claim: Al-Hawfi reports damma and fatha as dialect forms, with kasra also attested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r5.anchor: وقال الحوفي: والمكث بالضم والفتح لغتان، وقد قرىء بهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r6.claim: The Quran was revealed gradually in response to events, sayings, and actions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p124/r6.anchor: ونزلناه تنزيلا على حسب الحوادث من الأقوال والأفعال

ELMALILI:v1p102/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r1.claim: The Qur'an is the name of the manifest Book revealed in Arabic to Muhammad and transmitted to the community by tawātur.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r1.anchor: Kur’an: Allah teâlâ tarafından Resûl-i kibriyâsı Peygamberimiz

ELMALILI:v1p102/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r2.claim: In its original linguistic sense, qurʾān is a verbal noun on the pattern of ghufrān meaning recitation; the Book was named for its recited quality.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r2.anchor: Asl-ı lügatta Kur’an, “gufran” vezninde kıraat mânasına masdar idi

ELMALILI:v1p102/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r3.claim: The Qur'an is recited slowly with tartīl and tilāwa as 17:106, 13:30, and 73:4 state; Elmalılı connects this practice to its name.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r3.anchor: tertîl ve tilâvet ile kıraat olunmak olduğu cihetle buna “Kur’an” tesmiye buyurulmuştur

ELMALILI:v1p102/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r4.claim: God revealed the Qur'an truthfully to the Prophet's heart through Gabriel, also called the Trustworthy Spirit and the Holy Spirit, as affirmed in 2:97, 16:102, and 26:193–194.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r4.anchor: Cibrîl vâsıtasıyla hak olarak nâzil oldu

ELMALILI:v1p102/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r5.claim: Both the Qur'an's sending down and its descent occurred in truth, as 17:105 says.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r5.anchor: İndirilmesi de bihakkın, inmesi de bihakkın oldu

ELMALILI:v1p102/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r6.claim: It descended as an Arabic Qur'an without crookedness; what was not revealed as Qur'an is not called Qur'an.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r6.anchor: Hem hiç i‘vicâcsız Arabî Kur’an olarak nâzil oldu

ELMALILI:v1p102/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p102/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p102/r7.claim: The Prophet's explanations and hadiths are not Qur'an; nor is a ḥadīth qudsī Qur'an, because its wording was not revealed as Qur'anic composition.
ELMALILI:v1p102/r7.anchor: Peygamber’in tefsirlerine, hadislerine Kur’an denilmediği gibi

BURHAN:v1p236/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p236/r1.claim: The Companions gathered the revealed Qur’an between two covers without addition or loss because it had been scattered among palm stalks, stones, and memorized by people who might die; they wrote what they heard from the Prophet.
BURHAN:v1p236/r1.anchor: إثبات ظاهر أن الصحابة جمعوا بين الدفتين القرآن المنزل من غير زيادة ولا نقص والذى حملهم على جمعه

BURHAN:v1p236/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p236/r2.claim: The Prophet directed the Qur’an’s arrangement; the Companions gathered it in one place rather than determining its order, and revelation order differs from recitation order.
BURHAN:v1p236/r2.anchor: وهذا الترتيب كان منه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتوقيف لهم على ذلك وأن هذه الآية عقب تلك الآية فثبت أن سعى الصحابة فى جمعه فى موضع واحد لا فى ترتيب

BURHAN:v1p236/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p236/r3.claim: The Qur’an was placed in its present order in the Preserved Tablet and sent all at once to the lowest heaven, then revealed gradually to the Prophet as needs arose; the Companion consensus secured preservation, removed disagreement, and unified the community.
BURHAN:v1p236/r3.anchor: أن القرآن مكتوب فى اللوح المحفوظ على هذا الترتيب الذى هو فى مصاحفنا الآن أنزله الله جملة واحدة إلى سماء الدنيا

BURHAN:v1p236/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p236/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
BURHAN:v1p236/r4.claim: Al-Sulamī says the leading Companions shared the public recitation, the Prophet’s twice-yearly review with Gabriel in his final year; Zayd witnessed that final review, taught it, and was therefore chosen by Abū Bakr and tasked by ʿUthmān.
BURHAN:v1p236/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى كانت قراءة أبى بكر وعمر وعثمان وزيد بن ثابت والمهاجرين والأنصار واحدة

BURHAN:v1p236/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p236/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p236/r5.claim: Ibn Fāris distinguishes two compilations: the Companions arranged the suras, while the Prophet, by instruction, arranged the verses within each sura.
BURHAN:v1p236/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين بن فارس فى المسائل الخمس جمع القرآن على ضربين أحدهما تأليف السور

BURHAN:v1p259/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p259/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p259/r2.claim: Some interpret tartīl as reading the Qur’an in its given order without advancing or delaying; reversing it is condemned, and an oath to read it in order refers to this order.
BURHAN:v1p259/r2.anchor: أى اقرأه على هذا الترتيب من غير تقديم ولا تأخير وجاء النكير

BURHAN:v1p259/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p259/r3.claim: The suras and verses were revealed in stages to meet people’s changing needs; abrogating and abrogated material could not descend together, and gradual revelation’s chief wisdom is stated in this verse.
BURHAN:v1p259/r3.anchor: وإنما تفرقت سوره وآياته نزولا لحاجة الناس إليها حالة بعد حالة ولأن فيه الناسخ والمنسوخ

BURHAN:v1p259/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p259/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
BURHAN:v1p259/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr reports different early mushaf orders: some followed revelation chronology, ʿAlī began with Iqraʾ, Ibn Masʿūd with al-Fātiḥa then al-Baqara and al-Nisāʾ, and Ubayy with al-Fātiḥa then al-Nisāʾ and other suras.
BURHAN:v1p259/r4.anchor: فإن قيل قد اختلف السلف فى ترتيب القرآن فمنهم من كتب فى المصحف السور على تاريخ نزولها

BURHAN:v1p259/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p259/r5.speaker: مكي
BURHAN:v1p259/r5.claim: A proposed answer is that the Companions may have arranged the suras by their own judgment, while the Prophet placed the basmala at the beginning.
BURHAN:v1p259/r5.anchor: فالجواب أنه يحتمل أن يكون ترتيب السور على ما هى عليه اليوم على وجه الاجتهاد من الصحابة

BURHAN:v1p259/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p259/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
BURHAN:v1p259/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the Qur’an first descended whole to the lowest heaven, then over more than twenty years; Gabriel showed the Prophet each sura and verse’s placement, so the full arrangement comes from the Prophet and changing a sura’s place disrupts its order.
BURHAN:v1p259/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن الأنبارى أنزل الله القرآن كله إلى سماء الدنيا ثم فرق فى بضع وعشرين

BURHAN:v1p263/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r1.speaker: القتيبي
BURHAN:v1p263/r1.claim: Al-Qutaybī allows surah with or without hamza: with hamza he derives it from what remains in a vessel, making a sura a portion of the Qur’an; without hamza he relates it to the preceding sense.
BURHAN:v1p263/r1.anchor: قال القتيبى السورة تهمز ولا تهمز فمن همزها جعلها من أسأرت أى أفضلت من السور

BURHAN:v1p263/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p263/r2.claim: Some derive the word from a section of a building wall, with one level following another.
BURHAN:v1p263/r2.anchor: ومنهم من شبهها بسور البناء أى القطعة منه أي منزلة بعد منزلة

BURHAN:v1p263/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p263/r3.claim: Others derive surah from a city wall because it encloses and gathers its verses, comparing it also to a bracelet that surrounds the arm; on this account the wāw is original.
BURHAN:v1p263/r3.anchor: وقيل من سور المدينة لإحاطتها بآياتها واجتماعها كاجتماع البيوت بالسور

BURHAN:v1p263/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p263/r4.claim: Another possible derivation is rank, since verses are ordered appropriately within each sura; this supports studying correspondences between verses.
BURHAN:v1p263/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون من السورة بمعنى المرتبة لأن الآيات مرتبة فى كل سورة ترتيبا مناسبا

BURHAN:v1p263/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r5.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v1p263/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī connects surah with elevation of rank because it is God’s speech and contains lawful and forbidden matters, and also discusses derivation from a leap or rising.
BURHAN:v1p263/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جنى فى شرح منهوكة أبى نواس إنما سميت سورة لإرتفاع قدرها لأنها كلام الله تعالى

BURHAN:v1p263/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p263/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s plural is suwar with a short u, unlike the plural for a building wall, sūr with a short u in the plural’s second syllable.
BURHAN:v1p263/r7.anchor: وجمع سورة القرآن سور بفتح الواو وجمع سورة البناء سور بسكونها

BURHAN:v1p263/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p263/r8.claim: Some disliked saying a particular sura’s name, but the sound view permits it; Ibn Masʿūd’s phrase about the station of the one given al-Baqara is an example.
BURHAN:v1p263/r8.anchor: ثم كره بعضهم أن يقال سورة كذا والصحيح جوازه ومنه قول ابن مسعود هذا مقام الذى أنزلت عليه سورة البقرة

BURHAN:v1p263/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r9.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p263/r9.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī defines a sura technically as Qur’an consisting of verses with an opening and a closing, with three verses as its minimum.
BURHAN:v1p263/r9.anchor: فقال الجعبرى حد السورة قرآن يشتمل على آى ذوات فاتحة وخاتمة وأقلها ثلاث آيات

BURHAN:v1p263/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r10.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p263/r10.claim: Dividing the Qur’an into suras makes each sura, and each bounded verse, a distinct art and a sign; the range from short to long suras shows length is not required for inimitability, since al-Kawthar’s three verses match al-Baqara in miraculous character.
BURHAN:v1p263/r10.anchor: وفى تسوير السورة تحقيق لكون السورة بمجردها معجزة وآية من آيات الله تعالى وسورت السور طوالا وقصارا

BURHAN:v1p263/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p263/r11.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p263/r11.claim: Sura divisions help teach and memorize gradually: children celebrate finishing each short sura, reciters rest at its end, and each sura has an independent theme, such as Joseph’s story or the hypocrites in al-Tawba.
BURHAN:v1p263/r11.anchor: ثم ظهرت لذلك حكمة فى التعليم وتدريج الأطفال من السور القصار إلى ما فوقها يسيرا يسيرا

ITQAN:v1p117/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p117/r1.claim: The soundest and best-known view is that the Qur’an descended whole to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then gradually over twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years, depending on the disputed length of the Prophet’s Makkan residence after his mission.
ITQAN:v1p117/r1.anchor: أحدها وهو الأصح الأشهر أنه نزل إلى سماء الدنيا ليلة القدر جملة واحدة ثم نزل بعد ذلك منجما

ITQAN:v1p117/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Qur’an descended whole to the lowest heaven at the star positions, then God sent it to the Prophet piecemeal.
ITQAN:v1p117/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أنزل القرآن في ليلة القدر جملة واحدة إلى سماء الدنيا وكان بمواقع النجوم

ITQAN:v1p117/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r3.claim: In a report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says it descended to the lowest heaven on one night and was then revealed over twenty years; he cites the verse about answers to challenges and gradual recitation.
ITQAN:v1p117/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال أنزل القرآن في ليلة واحدة إلى السماء الدنيا ليلة القدر ثم أنزل بعد ذلك بعشرين سنة

ITQAN:v1p117/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r4.claim: The same Ibn Abbas report explains that when the polytheists raised a new matter, God revealed an answer concerning it.
ITQAN:v1p117/r4.anchor: فكان المشركون إذا أحدثوا شيئا أحدث الله لهم جوابا

ITQAN:v1p117/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Qur’an was separated from the Reminder, placed in the House of Might in the lowest heaven, and then brought down by Gabriel; al-Suyuti says all its chains are sound.
ITQAN:v1p117/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال فصل القرآن من الذكر فوضع في بيت العزة من السماء الدنيا فجعل جبريل ينزل به على النبي

ITQAN:v1p117/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r6.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the Qur’an descended whole to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan and was then sent down in portions; al-Suyuti grades its chain acceptable.
ITQAN:v1p117/r6.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس قال أنزل القرآن في ليلة القدر في شهر رمضان

ITQAN:v1p117/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p117/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p117/r7.claim: A further report says it was placed whole in the House of Might, then Gabriel brought it to Muhammad in response to people’s words and deeds.
ITQAN:v1p117/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني والبزار من وجه آخر عنه قال أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة حتى وضع في بيت العزة

ITQAN:v1p141/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p141/r1.speaker: الجاحظ
ITQAN:v1p141/r1.claim: Al-Jahiz says the whole revelation is called Qur’an, its divisions are surahs like poems, its verses are like poetic lines, and its closing pauses are like rhymes.
ITQAN:v1p141/r1.anchor: قال الجاحظ سمى الله كتابه اسما مخالفا لما سمى العرب كلامهم على الجملة والتفصيل سمى جملته قرآنا

ITQAN:v1p141/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p141/r2.speaker: أبو المعالي عزيزي بن عبد الملك المعروف بشيذلة
ITQAN:v1p141/r2.claim: Shidhla says the Qur’an has fifty-five names, including Book, Qur’an, Speech, Light, Guidance, Criterion, Healing, Reminder, Blessed, Wisdom, Rope, Best Discourse, Spirit, Revelation, Arabic, Truth, Astonishing, and Reminder.
ITQAN:v1p141/r2.anchor: وقال أبو المعالي عزيزي بن عبد الملك المعروف بشيذلة في كتاب البرهان اعلم أن الله سمى القرآن بخمسة وخمسين اسما

ITQAN:v2p317#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p317#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p317#2/r1.claim: In this Qur’anic glossary, farraqnāhu means that God made the revelation distinct or set it out in detail.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p179/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p179/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p179/r2.claim: The distinction between joining and separating clauses is especially subtle; merely calling a clause without a conjunction a fresh start does not explain the choice.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p179/r2.anchor: علم هذا الباب أغمض وأخفى وأدق وأصعب

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi says the Qur’an was revealed in separate installments and contains rulings and sciences, in keeping with the verse’s description of its gradual recitation.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r1.anchor: أنزله مفرقا نجوما وأودعه أحكاما وعلوما قال عز من قائل:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reports that revelation lasted eighteen years: eight in Mecca before the Hijra and ten in Medina.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r2.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول في قوله تعالى: {وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث} ذكر لنا أنه كان بين أوله وآخره ثماني عشرة سنة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r3.speaker: الشعبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi gives a different estimate of twenty or approximately twenty years and praises the Qur’an as a wise, miraculous guide that bears proofs, defeats falsehood, and strengthens Islam.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p7/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: فرق الله تنزيله فكان بين أوله وآخره عشرون أو نحو من عشرين سنة

DAMGHANI:v1p438/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r5.claim: Makth can mean doing something at leisure or without haste.
DAMGHANI:v1p438/r5.anchor: المكث اى على مهل . قوله تعالى فى سورة الإسراء

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r4.claim: Here tanzīl means clarification: God explained the Qur’an clearly.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r4.anchor: الرابع التنزيل بمعنى البيان قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء ونزلناه تنزيلا أي وبيناه بيانا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Qur’an was revealed a verse, two verses, or several at a time in response to their questions and as a reply to the Prophet; this is the meaning of its being sent down gradually.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r1.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق، عن معمر، عن قتادة، عن الحسن أنه قال في قول الله عز وجل: ورتلناه ترتيلا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r2.claim: The gradual sending down in 17:106 means the Qur’an came piece by piece.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p151/r2.anchor: وكذلك معنى قوله سبحانه: ونزلناه تنزيلا [الإسراء: 106] شيئا بعد شيء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r1.claim: In revelation order, ten letter-opened suras preceded al-Qasas: the first began with nūn and the tenth with ṭā-sīn-mīm.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r1.anchor: بعد أن نزلت عشر سور مفتتحة بالحروف المقطعة أولاها "ن" وعاشرتُها سورة القصص المفتتحة بـ "طسم"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r2.claim: Al-Isra, fiftieth in revelation order, answers the polytheists' challenge and their demands for other signs to prove a human messenger.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r2.anchor: نزلت سورة الإسراء - الخمسون في ترتيب النزول - تواجههم بصريح المعاجزة بمثل هذا القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r3.claim: The gradual recitation in 17:106 follows the sura's challenge and its account of the deniers' demands; the surrounding passage then affirms that the Qur'an came down in truth.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r4.claim: The Qur'an is the clear Arabic miracle: its Arab hearers know that humans and the jinn who assist them cannot produce its like.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p168/r4.anchor: هو بشر رسول، معجزته هذا الكتاب العربي المبين، يعرف الذين نزل بلسانهم كما لا يعرف سواهم من غير العرب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابثباتالياءوالواوفيالهاءال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابثباتالياءوالواوفيالهاءال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابثباتالياءوالواوفيالهاءال.claim: When a long vowel precedes pronominal hāʾ, dropping its following yāʾ or wāw in connected speech is preferred; Sībawayh favors these shortened readings but accepts full realization as Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابثباتالياءوالواوفيالهاءال.anchor: فلما اجتمعت حروف متشابهة حذفوا وهو أحسن وأكثر

NASHR:v1p414/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p414/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p414/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr transfers the hamza’s vowel in these Quran forms, including Quran al-fajr, qurʾānan farraqnāhu, and fa-ttabiʿ qurʾānahu.

NASHR:v1p450/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p450/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p450/r1.claim: In some rasm forms, وقرآنا فرقناه and قرآنا عربيا is abbreviated with the letters qāf-rā-nūn; other alifs are omitted for lightness.
NASHR:v1p450/r1.anchor: وكذلك حذف في بعضها من وقرآنا فرقناه في سبحان

NASHR:v2p63/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says al-Yazīdī's unqualified fatḥ of الناس would not prove that form or invalidate contrary transmission; al-Yazīdī's book indicates his fatḥ was a personal choice.
NASHR:v2p63/r1.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن الفتح اختيار منه

NASHR:v2p63/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن داود الحربي
NASHR:v2p63/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarbī reports from Abū ʿAmr that imāla of الناس in the genitive is a Hijazi dialect and that Abū ʿAmr used it; al-Hudhali also transmits it through al-Dūrī and others.
NASHR:v2p63/r2.anchor: ذكر عبد الله بن داود الحربي عن أبي عمرو أن الإمالة في الناس في موضع الخفض

NASHR:v2p63/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63/r3.claim: Most transmitters and regional reader communities report fatḥ for Abū ʿAmr; only two Yazīdī routes explicitly transmit imāla, but Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both from al-Dūrī and has read both.
NASHR:v2p63/r3.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عندنا من رواية الدوري عن أبي عمرو

NASHR:v2p72/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p72/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الشذائي، وأبو الحسن بن المنادي، وابن حبش
NASHR:v2p72/r1.claim: One group opens words such as الناس when stopping with sukūn, reasoning that the kasra causing imāla has disappeared; they also report this approach from Basran readers and particular routes from Warsh and Hamza.
NASHR:v2p72/r1.anchor: وهذا مذهب أبي بكر الشذائي وأبي الحسن بن المنادي وابن حبش

NASHR:v2p72/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p72/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v2p72/r2.claim: The majority preserve full imāla or the between-between form at pause, since pause is incidental and the word's original connecting form was imāla; this is the dominant teaching and practice.
NASHR:v2p72/r2.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى أن الوقف على ذلك في مذهب من أمال

NASHR:v2p72/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p72/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p72/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says both stop forms are sound from al-Sūsī and that he read both; he limits the fatḥ-only report to particular routes, while the prevalent practice sustains imāla.
NASHR:v2p72/r3.anchor: وكلا الوجهين صحيحان عن السوسي نصا وأداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r6.claim: In the Kashshaf preface, al-Zamakhshari pairs أنزل and نزله to express gradual, repeated revelation, matching the intensive force of نزّل.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r6.anchor: ولذلك قال العلامة الزمخشري في خطبة الكشاف الحمد لله الذي أنزل القرآن كلاما مؤلفا منظما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur says intensification from a transitive geminate is a pragmatic implication: choosing its heavier form over hamza signals abundance, reinforced by pairing both forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r7.anchor: وأنا أرى أن استفادة معنى التكثير في حال استعمال التضعيف للتعدية أمر من مستتبعات الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r11.claim: فرقناه in 17:106 is read with either a light or doubled consonant; 2:285 also uses the light form لا نفرق.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r11.anchor: كقوله تعالى ) وقرآنا فرقناه ( قرىء بالتشديد والتخفيف

JISHUMI:v1p195/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r1.claim: Qurʾān means “collection”; qaraʾa means to recite, and a basin is called miqrāh because water gathers in it.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r1.anchor: وللقرآن أسام فمنها: القرآن، ومعناه الجمع،

JISHUMI:v1p195/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r2.claim: Furqān may mean salvation and escape, or the distinction between truth and falsehood, the latter attributed to Ibn al-ʿAbbās.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r2.anchor: ومنها: الفرقان، قيل: معناه أنه النجاة والمخرج، ومنه: (يجعل لكم فرقانا)

JISHUMI:v1p195/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v1p195/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says he received the seven long sūras instead of the Torah, the seven mathānī instead of the Gospel, the hundreds instead of the Psalms, and was favored with the mufassal.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r4.anchor: وروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطوال،

JISHUMI:v1p195/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r5.claim: The long sūras include al-Baqara through al-Tawba, though another count extends them to the end of Sūrat Yūsuf.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r5.anchor: فالطوال: البقرة، وآل عمران، والنساء، والمائدة، والأنعام، والأعراف، والتوبة،

JISHUMI:v1p195/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r6.claim: Mathānī are sūras exceeding one hundred verses because rulings recur in them, or they are al-Fātiḥa; miʾūn are sūras around one hundred verses.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r6.anchor: والمثاني: ما زاد على مائة آية، لأنه تثنى فيها الأحكام، وقيل: الفاتحة،

JISHUMI:v1p195/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r7.claim: The mufassal are short sūras, named for the many divisions between them.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r7.anchor: والمفصل: السور القصار، لكثرة الفصول بين السور.

JISHUMI:v1p195/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r8.claim: Sūra is pluralized as suwar; without hamza it means an elevated dwelling, while some hamz it for a Qur’anic section; suʾr means a remainder.

JISHUMI:v1p195/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r9.claim: Āya may mean a sign marking the beginning and end of speech or a group of letters, as in “the people came with their group.”
JISHUMI:v1p195/r9.anchor: فأما الآية فقيل: معناها العلامة، سميت بذلك لدلالتها على أول الكلام

JISHUMI:v1p195/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r10.speaker: سيبويه
JISHUMI:v1p195/r10.claim: Sībawayh assigns wāw to the middle root position in āya because roots with medial wāw and final yā are more common than roots with both positions yā.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r10.anchor: وقال سيبويه: موضع العين من الآية واو؛ لأن ما كان موضع العين منه واوا

JISHUMI:v1p195/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r11.claim: Āya is also analyzed as having the morphological pattern faʿla or fāʿila.

JISHUMI:v1p195/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r12.claim: Tafsīr is uncovering what is covered; Abū al-ʿAbbās treats tafsīr, taʾwīl, and meaning as synonyms.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r12.anchor: أما التفسير، فالتفسير: كشف المغطى، قال أبو العباس: التفسير والتأويل

JISHUMI:v1p195/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r13.claim: Another definition says tafsīr explains obscure wording, while taʾwīl selects the interpretation that accords with the apparent sense; tafsīr is also clarification.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r13.anchor: وقال غيره: التفسير: كشف المراد عن اللفظ المشكل، والتأويل: رد أحد المحتملين

JISHUMI:v1p195/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r14.claim: Another view derives taʾwīl from a thing’s end or destination, citing “await only its interpretation.”
JISHUMI:v1p195/r14.anchor: وقيل: التأويل: انتهاء الشيء ومصيره، وما يؤول إليه أمره، ومنه: (هل ينظرون إلا تأويله)
